sideEffects: A possible treatment-related effect includes central Nervous System - Drowsiness is the most prominent CNS effect of this drug.
Some patients report sedation, somnolence, blurred vision, dizziness while taking this medicine.
Some patients report confusion, disorientation, and extrapyramidal symptoms such as oculogyric crisis, torticollis, and tongue protrusion while taking this medicine.

Some patients report lassitude, tinnitus, incoordination, fatigue, euphoria, nervousness, diplopia, insomnia, tremors, convulsive seizures, excitation, catatonic-like states.. while taking this medicine.
A possible treatment-related effect includes cardiovascular - Increased or decreased blood pressure, tachycardia, bradycardia, faintness.
Monitoring is advised because dermatologic - Dermatitis, photosensitivity, urticaria may occur.
Some patients report hematologic - Leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, thrombocytopenic purpura, agranulocytosis while taking this medicine.
Monitoring is advised because gastrointestinal - Dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, jaundice may occur.
seriousSideEffects: Healthcare providers evaluate risk when respiratory - Asthma, nasal stuffiness, respiratory depression (potentially fatal) and apnea (potentially fatal).

warnings.pregnancy: Extra caution is needed because pregnancy: Teratogenic Effects: Teratogenic effects have not been demonstrated in rat-feeding studies at doses of 6.25 and 12.5 mg/kg of promethazine.
warnings.breastfeeding: Healthcare providers evaluate risk when nursing Mothers - It is not known whether promethazine HCl is excreted in human milk.
warnings.kidney: Kidney function can influence clearance; nephrology input may be required for advanced renal impairment.
warnings.liver: Hepatic impairment may require dose changes and periodic liver function monitoring.
warnings.alcohol: Alcohol may amplify sedation or liver stress; avoid unless your clinician approves.
warnings.driving: Avoid driving if dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision occurs after dosing.

food: Take exactly as directed with respect to meals unless your prescriber advises otherwise.

storage: In routine practice, store refrigerated between 2°-8°C (36°-46°F).

faqs.question: Can I rely on this Promethazine hydrochloride information instead of a doctor visit?
faqs.answer: No. This content supports learning and preparation for conversations with qualified healthcare professionals. It is not a substitute for diagnosis or treatment.

faqs.question: Can I adjust the dose of Promethazine hydrochloride on my own?
faqs.answer: Dose changes should only be made with clinician guidance. Self-adjustment can increase side effects or reduce effectiveness.
